cases.sentence: Ночь, проведенная Левином на ___, не прошла для него даром.
options: копна
копны
копне
копной
cases.translation: The night Levin spent on the haystack was not wasted on him.
cases.explain: The preposition на (on) governs the prepositional case here, expressing location.

cases.sentence: Стоило ему ослабить энергию, и ему бы не достало ___ расплачиваться с рабочими.
options: деньги
денег
деньгам
деньгами
cases.translation: If he relaxed his effort, he would not have had enough money to pay the workers.
cases.explain: The construction не достало (there was not enough) requires the genitive case for the noun it applies to.

cases.sentence: На другой день, передав все опостылевшее хозяйство приказчику, уехал в дальний уезд к ___ своему Свияжскому.
options: приятель
приятеля
приятелю
приятелем
cases.translation: The next day, having handed over the whole loathsome estate to his steward, he set off for a distant district to his friend Sviyazhsky's.
cases.explain: The preposition к (to) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Дарья Александровна прислала ему ___, прося у него дамское седло для Кити.
options: записка
записки
записку
запиской
cases.translation: Darya Aleksandrovna sent him a note, asking him for a lady's saddle for Kitty.
cases.explain: Записку is the direct object of прислала (sent), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Он послал седло без ответа и с ___, что он сделал что-то стыдное.
options: сознание
сознания
сознанию
сознанием
cases.translation: He sent the saddle without a reply, with the awareness that he had done something shameful.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case here.

cases.sentence: ___ неудачи этой враждебности была теперь совершенно понятна ему.
options: причина
причины
причине
причиной
cases.translation: The cause of the failure and this hostility was now completely clear to him.
cases.explain: Причина is the subject of была (was), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Теперь же он рад был уехать и от соседств Щербатских, и, главное, от ___ именно на охоту.
options: хозяйство
хозяйства
хозяйству
хозяйством
cases.translation: Now he was glad to get away, both from the Shcherbatskys' neighborhood and, above all, from farming, off to the hunt.
cases.explain: The preposition от (from/away from) governs the genitive case.

reading.ru: Ночь, проведенная Левином на копне, не прошла для него даром.
reading.question: What effect did the night Levin spent on the haystack have on him?
options: It was not wasted on him — it changed his outlook
It left him exhausted and ill
It had no effect at all
It made him decide to sell his land
reading.correct: It was not wasted on him — it changed his outlook
reading.explain: The text states plainly that the night on the haystack was not wasted on him.

reading.ru: То хозяйство, которое он вел, опротивило ему и потеряло для него всякий интерес.
reading.question: How did Levin now feel about the farming he had been managing?
options: It disgusted him and had lost all interest for him
It excited him more than ever
He felt indifferent about it
He felt proud of his achievements
reading.correct: It disgusted him and had lost all interest for him
reading.explain: The estate management he had been carrying on had become repugnant to him and lost all interest.

reading.ru: Несмотря на превосходный урожай, никогда не было или, по крайней мере, никогда ему не казалось, чтобы было столько неудач и столько враждебных отношений между им и мужиками, как нынешний год.
reading.question: What was unusual about this year's harvest situation, despite an excellent crop?
options: There had never seemed to be so many failures and hostile relations with the peasants
The harvest itself had failed completely
The peasants had gone on strike
He had lost most of his land
reading.correct: There had never seemed to be so many failures and hostile relations with the peasants
reading.explain: Despite the excellent harvest, there had never before seemed to be so many failures and so much hostility between him and the peasants as this year.

reading.ru: Он ясно видел теперь, что то хозяйство, которое он вел, была только жестокая и упорная борьба между им и работниками.
reading.question: What did Levin now clearly see about the farming he managed?
options: That it was really just a harsh, stubborn struggle between him and the workers
That it was a partnership of shared interests
That it had always run smoothly
That the workers respected his methods
reading.correct: That it was really just a harsh, stubborn struggle between him and the workers
reading.explain: He now clearly saw that the farming he had been running was nothing but a cruel, stubborn struggle between himself and the laborers.

reading.ru: Он стоял за каждый свой грош и не мог не стоять, потому что стоило ему ослабить энергию, и ему бы не достало денег расплачиваться с рабочими.
reading.question: Why did Levin have to fight for every penny?
options: Because if he relaxed, he would not have enough money to pay the workers
Because the workers demanded higher wages
Because he wanted to save for Kitty
Because his brother controlled the finances
reading.correct: Because if he relaxed, he would not have enough money to pay the workers
reading.explain: He had to fight for every penny because if he let up his effort, he would not have enough money to pay the laborers.

reading.ru: Работнику же хотелось работать как можно приятнее, с отдыхом и, главное, беззаботно и забывшись, не размышляя.
reading.question: What did the workers want from their labor, according to the text?
options: To work as pleasantly as possible, with rest and without thinking
To finish quickly and go home early
To be paid in advance
To work harder than Levin expected
reading.correct: To work as pleasantly as possible, with rest and without thinking
reading.explain: The worker wanted to work as pleasantly as possible, with rest, and above all carelessly, without reflecting.

reading.ru: Он посылал скосить клевер на сено, выбрав плохие десятины, проросшие травой и полынью, негодные на семена.
reading.question: What did Levin order regarding the clover fields, and what happened instead?
options: He chose the poor plots to be mown, but the best seed plots were mown instead
He ordered all fields mown at once
He forbade any mowing that season
He mowed the fields himself
reading.correct: He chose the poor plots to be mown, but the best seed plots were mown instead
reading.explain: He ordered the poor, weedy plots unfit for seed to be mown, but the best seed plots were mown instead because they were easier to cut.

reading.ru: И Ванька, проработав весь день, заснул и каялся в своем грехе, говоря «воля ваша».
reading.question: What happened with Vanka, who was supposed to guard the horses at night?
options: After working all day, he fell asleep and repented, saying "as you wish"
He refused to work at all
He successfully guarded the horses all night
He quit his job in protest
reading.correct: After working all day, he fell asleep and repented, saying "as you wish"
reading.explain: Vanka, having worked all day, fell asleep on watch and repented his fault, saying "as you wish."

reading.ru: Уже давно Левин чувствовал недовольство своим отношением к хозяйству.
reading.question: How long had Levin felt dissatisfaction with his approach to farming?
options: For a long time already
Only since that morning
He had never felt dissatisfied before this night
Since his engagement was broken
reading.explain: The text says Levin had long felt dissatisfaction with his relationship to his farming.

reading.ru: К этому еще присоединилось присутствие в тридцати верстах от него Кити Щербатской, которую он хотел и не мог видеть.
reading.question: What added to Levin's distress besides his troubles with farming?
options: The presence of Kitty Shcherbatskaya thirty versts away, whom he wanted but could not see
News of his brother's illness
A dispute with Sviyazhsky
The loss of his hunting dog
reading.correct: The presence of Kitty Shcherbatskaya thirty versts away, whom he wanted but could not see
reading.explain: Adding to his troubles was the presence, thirty versts away, of Kitty Shcherbatskaya, whom he wanted to see but could not.

reading.ru: Сам Левин, увидав Китти Щербатскую, понял, что он не переставал любить ее.
reading.question: What did Levin realize about his feelings for Kitty?
options: That he had never stopped loving her
That he no longer cared for her at all
That he loved her sister more
That his feelings had changed to friendship only
reading.correct: That he had never stopped loving her
reading.explain: Seeing Kitty Shcherbatskaya, Levin himself understood that he had never stopped loving her.

reading.ru: «Я не могу просить ее быть моею женою, потому только что она не может быть женой того, кого она хотела», — говорил он сам себе.
reading.question: Why did Levin tell himself he could not ask Kitty to marry him?
options: Because she could not be the wife of the man she had actually wanted
Because his family disapproved of her
Because he had no money
Because Kitty had already married someone else
reading.correct: Because she could not be the wife of the man she had actually wanted
reading.explain: He told himself he could not ask her to be his wife simply because she could not be the wife of the man she had wanted (Vronsky).

reading.ru: Дарья Александровна прислала ему записку, прося у него дамское седло для Кити.
reading.question: What did Darya Aleksandrovna's note ask of Levin?
options: To borrow a lady's saddle for Kitty
To visit her that evening
To lend her some money
To help with the farm accounts
reading.correct: To borrow a lady's saddle for Kitty
reading.explain: Darya Aleksandrovna sent him a note asking to borrow a lady's saddle for Kitty.

reading.ru: Он написал десять записок и все разорвал, и послал седло без всякого ответа.
reading.question: How did Levin respond to Darya Aleksandrovna's request?
options: He wrote and tore up ten notes, then sent the saddle without any reply
He refused to send the saddle at all
He replied with a long letter explaining himself
He delivered the saddle in person
reading.correct: He wrote and tore up ten notes, then sent the saddle without any reply
reading.explain: He wrote ten notes and tore them all up, sending the saddle without any answer.

reading.ru: Дупелины и болота в Суровском уезде давно соблазняли Левина, но он за хозяйственными делами все откладывал эту поездку.
reading.question: Why had Levin not yet visited Sviyazhsky's hunting grounds?
options: He had kept postponing the trip because of his farm business
He did not enjoy hunting
Sviyazhsky had never invited him before
The marshes had dried up long ago
reading.correct: He had kept postponing the trip because of his farm business
reading.explain: The snipe grounds and marshes in the Surovsky district had long tempted Levin, but he kept putting off the trip because of his farm affairs.
